title: Watching a run after you go down
target: How to stay useful in R.E.P.O. once you are spectating rather than playing, using the player list, the voice channel and the extraction readout.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A headset if you want to talk
The understanding that the crew can still finish without you

steps.do: Expect to keep watching rather than dropping out of the run.
steps.because: the game keeps a flag for a player spectating rather than playing (isSpectate)

steps.do: Use the menu's player list to see who is still up.
steps.because: the menu can list players, and each listed entry has a name and a head of its own (MenuPlayerListed, playerName, playerHead)

steps.do: Read the connection figure on a row rather than guessing who is lagging.
steps.because: a row carries a ping figure as text (pingText)

steps.do: Watch the crowning on a row, and know it can be forced.
steps.because: a row can be crowned on the left and on the right, and a crown can be forced onto it (leftCrown, rightCrown, forceCrown)

steps.do: Make your own row readable so the crew can find you at a glance.
steps.because: a listed name can be drawn bright (brightName)

steps.do: Keep talking, because voice is part of the same networking the run uses.
steps.because: voice comes through the game's networking library with a voice box of its own (VoiceBox, Photon.Voice.Unity)

steps.do: Watch extraction readiness rather than asking whether it is time to leave.
steps.because: readiness is a state with flags and a localised label of its own (ExtractReady, OpenToExtractReady, localizedExtractionReady)

steps.do: Remember the lobby can keep the kinds of lobby you have saved.
steps.because: the game keeps lobby types that have been saved and a lobby menu of its own (LobbyMenu, Lobby, savedLobbyTypes)

commonMistakes: Sitting silent because you are not the one holding the valuables.
Guessing who is lagging instead of reading the row.
Missing that the crew is extraction-ready because you were watching the wrong thing.
Dropping out of the run rather than spectating the rest of it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
